plan.contextChunk: This figure combines a ray construction with an intensity curve for light passing through a single slit. At the left a vertical tan barrier is drawn in two segments with a narrow gap between them; a double-headed arrow spans the gap and a curved arrow connects it to the label a. A short teal arrow labeled lambda enters horizontally from the left and reaches the opening. From the slit five gray dashed lines fan out to the right toward a vertical gray line labeled Screen, and the middle dashed line runs straight along the horizontal. Two arcs measure angles from that horizontal reference: the outer upper line is marked theta_2 = 45 degrees and the inner upper line is marked theta_1 = ?, with two more dashed lines mirroring them below the axis. Drawn on the screen is a red wavy curve, tied by a curved arrow to the label Intensity on screen, whose sideways excursion represents brightness; it has a tall broad central peak on the axis and smaller lobes above and below, and each dashed ray meets the screen exactly where the curve pinches in to nothing. Lining the ray directions up with the nulls of the curve identifies each dashed line with a numbered diffraction minimum, so that the known 45 degree direction can be used to recover the slit width a and then the unknown angle theta_1.

interactionPlan.concept: For a single slit, the dark fringes occur at angles satisfying a·sinθ = mλ, so the geometric directions of the dashed rays coincide exactly with the zeros of the intensity pattern on the screen, and the angular spread of the pattern grows with λ/a.
elements: Vertical tan barrier drawn as two thick segments (upper and lower) on the left with a narrow gap between them
Double-headed black arrow spanning the gap, marking the slit opening
Curved black arrow from the double-headed arrow to the italic label 'a' at far left
Short horizontal teal arrow entering from the left toward the slit, labeled 'λ'
Horizontal gray dashed central axis running from the slit to the screen (θ = 0, central maximum direction)
Two upper gray dashed rays fanning out from the slit to the screen (first and second minima)
Two lower gray dashed rays mirroring them below the axis
Angle arc from the axis to the outer upper ray, labeled 'θ₂ = 45°'
Smaller angle arc from the axis to the inner upper ray, labeled 'θ₁ = ?'
Vertical gray line on the right labeled 'Screen' at its top
Red wavy intensity curve drawn sideways along the screen: tall broad central lobe on the axis, smaller secondary lobes above and below, pinching to zero exactly where each dashed ray meets the screen
Curved black arrow from the lower part of the red curve to the label 'Intensity on screen'
Order labels m = ±1, m = ±2 placed near where each dashed ray meets the screen
Readout panel showing current a, λ, a/λ, and the computed θ₁ and θ₂

interactions.teaches: Narrowing the slit pushes the minima to larger angles and widens the central bright band — angular spread is inversely proportional to slit width.
interactions.label: Slit width a (nm)

interactions.teaches: Longer wavelengths diffract more: every minimum angle grows with λ, so the whole pattern stretches outward while the order structure stays the same.
interactions.label: Wavelength λ (nm)

interactions.teaches: Each dashed ray direction is not decorative — clicking it locks together the geometric angle θ_m and the exact point where the red intensity curve collapses to zero, making a·sinθ = mλ concrete.

demo_steps.title: The given configuration
demo_steps.narration: Light of wavelength λ passes a slit of width a and fans out into five marked directions. The outermost upper ray is the second minimum at θ₂ = 45°; the inner one is the unknown θ₁.

demo_steps.title: Rays meet the nulls
demo_steps.narration: Click any dashed ray: it lights up together with the point where the red curve pinches to zero. Every dashed line points at a dark fringe, never a bright one.

demo_steps.title: Solve for θ₁
demo_steps.narration: With a·sin45° = 2λ fixing a ≈ 2.83λ, the m = 1 condition a·sinθ₁ = λ gives sinθ₁ = 0.354, so θ₁ ≈ 20.7° — read it off the inner arc.

demo_steps.title: Narrow the slit
demo_steps.narration: Shrink a while λ stays fixed: the dashed rays swing outward and the central lobe balloons. A smaller opening produces a wider diffraction pattern.

demo_steps.title: Widen the slit
demo_steps.narration: Open the slit up and the rays collapse toward the axis, the central peak narrows, and the light behaves more like a straight beam.

demo_steps.title: Change the color
demo_steps.narration: Back at the original width, switch from blue to red light: longer λ pushes every null to a larger angle. Only the ratio λ/a controls the pattern.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The dashed rays and the zeros of the red curve are the same physics seen two ways — a·sinθ = mλ means the pattern's angular size is set entirely by the ratio λ/a.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Landscape layout. Left third: two thick tan vertical bars with a small gap; a black double-headed arrow across the gap, a curved arrow to the italic label 'a' at the far left edge; a short teal horizontal arrow labeled 'λ' entering the slit. Right edge: a vertical medium-gray line labeled 'Screen' at top. From the slit, five thin gray dashed lines fan symmetrically to the screen — the middle one horizontal, two above and two below at the m = 1 and m = 2 minimum angles. Two thin arcs centered at the slit measure from the horizontal to the upper rays, labeled 'θ₂ = 45°' (outer) and 'θ₁ = ?' (inner). The red intensity curve is drawn sideways along the screen line: excursion to the left (or right) of the line represents brightness, with a tall wide central lobe on the axis and progressively smaller lobes above and below; it must touch zero precisely where each dashed ray lands. A curved black arrow from the lower curve points to the label 'Intensity on screen'. Selected minima highlight in a saturated accent (e.g., orange) on both the dashed ray and the null point, with a small badge showing m and θ. Keep a compact readout of a, λ, a/λ, θ₁, θ₂ in a corner. When sliders make sinθ_m exceed 1, that order should visibly disappear from both the fan and the curve.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for slit width a: learner changes the opening while lambda stays fixed; the dashed minimum directions and red intensity nulls spread apart or compress; the inverse relationship between slit width and diffraction-pattern angular spacing becomes clear.
- Slider for wavelength lambda: learner changes the incoming wavelength; the intensity lobes and minimum angles shift outward for longer wavelengths and inward for shorter ones; the condition a sin(theta)=m lambda becomes visible on the screen.

authoredContext:
Calculating Single-Slit Diffraction Visible light of wavelength 550 nm falls on a single slit and produces its second diffraction minimum at an angle of 45.0° relative to the incident direction of the light, as in the figure. (a) What is the width of the slit? (b) At what angle is the first minimum produced?

In this example, we analyze a graph of the single-slit diffraction pattern.

Figure shows a vertical line on the left. This has a slit in the middle, of length a. A ray labeled lambda passes horizontally through the slit. This splits into 5 dotted lines that fall on a screen. The screen is shown as a vertical line. Of the five dotted lines, two make angles theta 1 and theta 2 with the horizontal. Theta 2 is 45 degrees. Theta 1 is smaller than theta 2 and is unknown. Intensity on the screen is shown as a vertical wave. The crest at the center, where a horizontal dotted line from the center of the slit falls on the screen, is the largest. The wave attenuates at the top and bottom. The remaining four dotted lines correspond to troughs in the wave.

Strategy From the given information, and assuming the screen is far away from the slit, we can use the equation asinθ=mλ first to find D, and again to find the angle for the first minimum θ1.

discrepancies: Intensity curve shape: the source draws a stylized wave whose side lobes are nearly as large as the central one and which visibly oscillates across the screen line; the generated sinc² has an exaggerated central lobe (165 px) with side lobes so small they collapse onto the screen line, so the top/bottom wiggles of the original are essentially absent.

Added elements not in the source: an 'm = ±1 / ±2' badge next to each null, white circular markers at the ray–screen intersections, and a floating a/λ/θ readout box in the upper-left corner — extra chrome that changes the look of the original clean diagram.

The 'Intensity on screen' callout is a long, nearly straight black line whose arrowhead lands next to the m = −2 marker/dot rather than a short curved squiggle touching the red curve as in the source, causing a mild collision with the m = −2 label.

Outer dashed rays in the source run past the screen edge (bottom-right ray exits below the screen line); in the generated figure all four rays terminate exactly on the screen line, slightly reducing the 'fan' impression.
Slit-width double arrow is placed left of the barrier centre and is crossed by the incoming λ arrow, whereas the source places the arrow neatly at the gap with the λ arrow stopping short of it.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful and physically correct reproduction of the single-slit diffraction figure (θ₂ = 45°, θ₁ = ? correctly resolving to 20.7°) with excellent sliders/step-demo/click interactions, but the intensity curve's side lobes are far flatter than the stylized source wave and several added badges/readout boxes plus a misaimed callout arrow clutter the composition.
action_items: Rescale or compress the intensity curve (e.g. plot √I or reduce central amplitude and boost side-lobe visibility) so the top and bottom oscillations of the source wave are clearly visible along the screen.
Redraw the 'Intensity on screen' callout as a short curved arrow whose tip touches the red curve near the bottom, and shift it clear of the m = −2 marker/label.
Tone down or make optional the extra chrome (m = ±n badges, white null dots, a/λ readout panel) so the default step-0 state reads as a drop-in replacement for the static source figure.
Move the slit-width double arrow to sit at the gap in the barrier and shorten the incoming λ arrow so the two no longer overlap.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; all action items are concrete rendering fixes (curve scaling, callout arrow placement, removing extra chrome, arrow positioning) that belong to the generator.

discrepancies: Intensity-curve shape differs in character: the source draws lobes of roughly comparable excursion filling the full screen height, while the generated curve (gamma-compressed sinc²) shows one dominant central lobe with much smaller side lobes and covers a shorter span of the screen line — recognizable, but the visual rhythm of the source is not reproduced.

The barrier gap is much tighter than in the source: the two tan bars are nearly touching and the slit-width double arrow sits on top of the gap, so the 'a' dimension reads as a single vertical bar rather than the clearly separated bars with an arrow between them.
Incident beam and λ label are rendered teal (wavelength-mapped colour for 500 nm) instead of the source's saturated blue arrow; small but noticeable colour shift on a prominent element.
Control-panel label text wraps badly ('Slit width a : 1414 nm' broken over five lines), which looks unpolished next to the otherwise clean figure.

Minor: the source's red curve crosses above/below the drawn screen segment ends, whereas here both the screen line and curve terminate short of the frame, giving slightly more empty margin top and bottom.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-labelled reconstruction of the single-slit diffraction geometry with physically correct a·sinθ = mλ coupling between dashed rays and the intensity nulls, plus a rich and genuinely pedagogical set of interactions; main weaknesses are the visually tight slit gap, a side-lobe amplitude profile that reads differently from the source's wave, and sloppy control-label wrapping.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, no failure modes), but concrete rendering issues — tight slit gap, side-lobe amplitude profile, beam colour, and wrapped control labels — are implementation-level fixes.

The 'Intensity on screen' callout is drawn as a long, almost straight leader line running far to the right of the screen, whereas the source uses a short S-curved arrow hooking up from the label into the bottom of the red curve.

The tan barrier renders as an almost continuous vertical bar: the slit gap and its double-headed dimension arrow are very small relative to the source, where the two separate bars and the gap between them are the dominant left-hand element.

Angle annotations θ₂ = 45° and θ₁ = ? are noticeably smaller and sit tighter to the rays than in the source, where they are large, prominent labels sitting in open space between the fan lines; the unicode subscripts render tiny at inline scale.

The italic 'a' callout arrow in the source terminates right at the slit's dimension arrow; in the generated version it stops short in empty space left of the barrier, so the label's referent is less clear.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and physically correct single-slit diffraction reproduction with an excellent set of meaningful interactions (slit-width and wavelength sliders, clickable minima rays tied to curve zeros, and a six-step guided derivation of θ₁ ≈ 20.7°); weaknesses are cosmetic — the intensity curve's lobe balance and the callout/barrier proportions drift from the source and the angle labels are somewhat undersized.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are sound (concept 5, interactivity 5) and the remaining issues are cosmetic rendering details — curve lobe proportions, callout leader geometry, barrier/slit scale, and undersized angle labels — which are generator-level fixes.
